newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares hit new record in high volume.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares hit new record in high volume.

text.p: 1545 GMT - Soaring pharmaceutical shares lifted Swiss share indices by more than one percent to a record close in high volumes.
Dealers said the U.S. employment cost index, which was below market expectations, and the firming U.S. dollar also gave shares a boost.
* The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 55.0 points, or 1.33 percent, to 4,182.3 points. The day's high was reached at 4,182.9.
* The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 34.16 points, or 1.29 percent, to 2,676.67 points.

* Most-active Roche certificates, which have been in the limelight in the past few sessions due to varied speculation about mergers or spin-offs, jumped 230 francs, or nearly two percent, to 12,010. One dealer said rumours that the company may launch a new drug triggered the rise.
Novartis registered shares rose 28 francs to 1,614. The company said 1996 group sales reached 36.23 billion francs vs 35.94 billion and that it expected a flat 1996 profit.
* Nestle, ABB, Holderbank, Surveillance and SMH were other clear winners in the blue-chip segment.
* UBS and Winterthur firmed more than one percent.
* Swissair continued its recent solid performance, climbing 34 francs, or 2.76 percent, to 1,267.
* Sulzer, Clariant and Swiss Re were among the few blue chips to post losses.
* Options on Novaratis were saught on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), dealers said.

Of a total 115,566 options traded, Sandoz accounted for 11,449 calls and 9,878 puts. The two Swiss pharmaceutical companies Sandoz and Ciba merged as Novartis in December, but options are still traded seperately.
Demand was also high for options on UBS, Winterthur and Nestle.
On the futures side, 4,452 SMI futures changed hands.
